result.topic_en: Draft passages arguing that the discontinuities of a function must be confined to isolated lines and points so that calculus can be applied, with a Dirichlet-type nowhere-continuous example. They then define a function of z = x+yi through the Cauchy–Riemann equations, exclude removable point discontinuities, and assume the surface T is simply connected and simply spread over the plane.
